messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Alert: high CPU on service=tokenizer-preproc in cluster=prod-us-east-1. 40% of pods OOMKilled in last 5m, node flaps detected. Auto-escalation to oncall.
Morgan: I’m paged, looking. Can someone dump recent pod events and top CPU pods?
Jamie: grabbing logs now. early signs look like a sudden prompt fanout — many small requests with huge tokenized expansions.
Alex: seeing repeated `killed: out of memory` in kubelet events for tokenizer-preproc-** pods. Also `oom_reaper` messages on nodes.
Priya: notable: two nodes in asg went NotReady then back. Prometheus shows CPU spike on the tokenizer-preproc deployment at 09:12 UTC from 15% -> 95% in ~30s.
Sofia: customer impact — Support dashboard shows increase in 502/504 for several teams and one premium tenant reports degraded throughput. Opening ticket INC-4987.
Morgan: good. Triage plan: 1) Mitigate customer impact (throttle /fall back), 2) stabilize cluster (drain/cordon affected nodes), 3) root cause (prompt flood / tokenizer hot-loop).
Jamie: quick mitigation: scale tokenizer-preproc to +3 replicas and temporarily set `max_concurrency=1` on deployment to reduce parallelism. Pushing patch now.
Alex: applying HPA override now: `kubectl scale deployment/tokenizer-preproc --replicas=8 -n inference`
Alex: also patching env: `kubectl set env deployment/tokenizer-preproc MAX_CONCURRENCY=1 -n inference`
Priya: running `kubectl get pods -o wide -n inference | grep tokenizer-preproc` and tailing logs:
```
kubectl describe pod tokenizer-preproc-7f8d9
Events:
  Warning  OOMKilled   2s  kubelet  Container killed due to out-of-memory
  Warning  BackOff     1s  kubelet  Back-off restarting failed container
```
Jamie: logs show repeated tokenization loops, example snippet:
```
[09:12:34] warn token_count=0 input_len=1200 -> tokens=24000
[09:12:34] error tokenizer: runaway token expansion during normalization, loop count=150
panic: runtime: out of memory
```
Morgan: that matches a bad prompt pattern — likely untrusted input causing extreme expansion. We should enable prefix/KV cache and reject suspicious normalization inputs at the edge. For now, can we add a request rate-limit per IP/customer at the edge LB?
Sofia: Support can apply a tenant-specific throttle for the affected premium account. Priya can you add a temporary rule in the rate limiter?
Priya: adding rule `limit: 10 req/s per tenant` for the affected tenant id: TID-9912. Pushed.
Alex: cordoning two flaky nodes now to stop scheduling: 
```
kubectl cordon ip-10-0-45-23.us-east-1
kubectl cordon ip-10-0-46-11.us-east-1
```
Then scheduling replacements via asg scale.

Jamie: restart plan for tokenizer-preproc pods (controlled): `kubectl rollout restart deployment/tokenizer-preproc -n inference` — doing a rolling restart to flush KV caches.
Morgan: make sure we keep 1 pod up per AZ during restart. Also set `terminationGracePeriodSeconds=60` to speed restarts.
Alex: restarted. Observability note: Prometheus alert `TokenizeCPUHigh` is silenced for 10m while we stabilize.
IncidentBot: Note: alert silenced by Morgan for 10m.
Sofia: customer update drafted: "We are investigating elevated errors affecting tokenization and are applying mitigations including rate limits and extra capacity. We'll update within 30 minutes." Ready to send once approved.
Morgan: send it, include link to ticket INC-4987 and ETA 30m.
Support: sent to the tenant and posted in status page.
Priya: after scaling and throttle, CPU dropped from 95% -> 45% on preproc. Pod restarts decreased. OOM events stopped after env change and restart.
Jamie: collecting heap/profile from one pod for postmortem: `kubectl exec -it tokenizer-preproc-xyz -- /bin/pprof --heap` saved to s3://redwood-incidents/4987/heap-0921.pb
Alex: digging into node-level logs — saw `kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 12345 (tokenizer) score 987` then `nv_peer_dev: GPU error` but gfx messages are noisy; primary was CPU oom.
Morgan: good containment. Next: temporarily add input sanitation at the API gateway to detect suspicious token blowups (max token multiplier 10x). Can eng-runtime own that quick patch?
Jamie: will open a small PR to the gateway with a hard cap and fallback to truncated prompt. Tagging `eng-runtime` and `devex` for reviews.
Sofia: Handoff note for next oncall (in 2h): changes made — scaled to 8 replicas, MAX_CONCURRENCY=1, rate limit for TID-9912, cordoned two nodes (ip-10-0-45-23, ip-10-0-46-11). Watch for new OOMs and node NotReady events.
Morgan: creating incident summary in the runbook channel and assigning action items:
- Jamie: collect profiles + sample problematic prompts (s3://redwood-incidents/4987/).
- Alex: confirm node stability and remove cordon when safe.
- Priya: keep throttle in place, consider global throttle if patterns repeat.
- Sofia: follow up with customer and close INC-4987 when stable.
Morgan: handing off to Alex for oncall rotation — I'll remain available for escalation. :wave:
Alex: acknowledged, I'll watch the cluster for 2h. Posting final status update in 10m.
Support: final customer note queued.
IncidentBot: Incident INC-4987 created and linked: https://incidents.internal/INC-4987
Morgan: closing thread here — moving to postmortem backlog once we have heap and prompt samples. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
